chunks: NPN vs PNP transistors. The question: What is the difference between an NPN and PNP?
NPN and PNP are the two flavors of bipolar junction transistor (BJT), a part that uses a small current to control a larger one. They do the same job with every polarity flipped.
An NPN switches on when its base is a little above its emitter, and a PNP switches on when its base is a little below its emitter.
Think of two doors that open in opposite directions. The NPN door opens when you push the base up above the emitter, and the PNP door when you pull it down below.
Both let a big flow through once open. The analogy breaks down on speed: electrons move more easily than holes, so the NPN is usually the faster, higher-gain door.
The NPN conducts when V in is more than 0. 7 volts above V out (sourcing current from +12 volts to the load); the PNP conducts when V in is more than 0.
7 volts below V out (sinking current to -12 volts). Between plus or minus 0. 7 volts neither conducts, which creates the dead zone and crossover distortion.
Base, emitter, collector: the three terminals. A small current at the base controls a larger current between collector and emitter.
Electrons and holes: the two kinds of charge carrier. A hole is a missing electron that acts like a moving positive charge.
Electrons do most of the carrying in an NPN, holes in a PNP. Forward-biased junction: a junction is the boundary between two differently treated silicon layers.
Forward-biased means pushed the way that lets current through, about 0. 7 volts for silicon.
Low-side / high-side switch: a switch placed between the load and ground, or between the supply and the load.
Put an NPN's emitter on ground. A base at 0 volts keeps it off, and a base at about 0. 7 volts or more starts to turn it on. Now put a PNP's emitter on a 5 volts supply.
A base at 5 volts keeps it off, and a base at about 4. 3 volts starts to turn it on. The NPN naturally sits on the ground side of a load, and the PNP on the supply side.
That is the whole idea.
"NPN and PNP are doping mirror images. NPN is N-P-N with electrons as main carriers; PNP is P-N-P with holes. An NPN conducts when the base is 0.
7 volts above the emitter, current flows into the collector and out of the emitter, and it's the natural low-side switch. A PNP conducts when the base is 0.
7 volts below the emitter, with current into the emitter, and it's the natural high-side switch.
Because holes are less mobile than electrons, PNPs are slower with lower gain, so NPNs are preferred when you have the choice."
